items.q: Is the sample really free? What's the catch?
items.a: Genuinely free. No card, no contract. We rebuild your homepage and show you. If you don't continue, you owe nothing — we just keep the work as a portfolio piece.

items.q: How can you do this in 48 hours when agencies take months?
items.a: Agencies bill discovery meetings, slide decks, and revisions. We use modern tooling to clone your structure, redesign the surface, and ship. Less theater, more output.

items.q: Will I lose my SEO rankings?
items.a: No. We preserve your URL structure, content, and metadata — and improve technical SEO on top. Clients gain rankings within 30 days.
Hosting, security patches, uptime monitoring, content updates (within reason), and minor design tweaks. Optional: €29/month flat, cancel anytime — or €0 if you prefer to run it yourself.

items.q: What if I want changes after seeing the sample?
items.a: That is the point of the sample. We discuss revisions in the contract phase, lock scope, and build the rest. No surprise invoices.
The free sample is your homepage — fastest way to show what we can do. The full rebuild covers your entire site.
Modern static-site stacks (Astro, Next.js) deployed on edge infrastructure. Translation: very fast, very cheap, very secure.

privacy.meta_description: What BetterSite collects when you request a free sample, and how it is used.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Short version: we ask only for what the sample needs, and one email deletes it all.

sections.body: The sample form asks for your current website URL and your email address. That is all — no account, no tracking pixels, no analytics on this site.
Your URL is what we rebuild; your email is where the live preview lands within 48 hours. If you do not continue, we keep nothing but the rebuild itself as a portfolio piece.
The form submits through Web3Forms, which delivers your request to our inbox. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. A bs_lang cookie remembers your language choice; nothing else is stored.
Email hello@bettersite.dev any time to see, correct or delete what we hold about you. No account to close, no data broker in the loop.

brand.meta_title: BetterSite brand identity: logo, colors, usage
brand.meta_description: The BetterSite logo explained: what the mark means, its colors and type, every logo file to download, and how to use it.
brand.title: One letter, before and after.
brand.lead: The BetterSite mark is a B built from two website blocks. The top one is the site you have today. The bottom one is the site we rebuild.

concept_parts.body: Your current website: a frame that still stands, drawn in warm stone grey.
Dated content inside it: a single bar, like an old layout waiting for work.
The rebuild: wider, filled, in our terracotta. Same foundation, better result.

brand.concept_body: Both blocks share one straight spine on the left, because we keep what works (your content, your name, your customers) and rebuild the rest. Read top to bottom, the B tells the whole service: before, then after.
brand.variants_note: All files are SVG vectors: sharp at any size, no fonts required.
brand.palette_title: Warm cream, steady navy, one terracotta accent

palette.name: Cream
palette.role: Page background: warm, like good paper

palette.name: Navy
palette.role: Headings, text and the word “Better”: the trust color

palette.name: Terracotta
palette.role: The “after”: the rebuilt bowl, “Site”, big highlights

palette.name: Terracotta dark
palette.role: Buttons, links and small accent text

brand.palette_note: Terracotta is the warm signal that means “better”. Keep it for the rebuilt bowl, buttons and key highlights; let cream and navy do the rest.
brand.type_body: The wordmark is set in Inter Bold with slightly tight letter-spacing, then converted to outlines so it looks identical everywhere. “Better” is set in navy; “Site” takes terracotta, so the name repeats the before-and-after of the mark.
rules: Leave clear space around the logo equal to the height of the top bowl.
Do not go below 20 px for the mark or 96 px wide for the full logo.
Use the files as they are: do not recolor, stretch, rotate or add effects.
On dark backgrounds, photos or color use the white logo; for one-color print use the black one.
